per_key_checks.prior_round_finding: E3C562B03258 F1 (major, terminology/consistency): asked for 'Actions pour {name}'
per_key_checks.assessment: Meaning preserved and now on the corpus's settled form. English 'Actions for {name}' is a neutral noun phrase naming the asset whose actions menu opens (it is an aria-label on the overflow trigger's Button in supplement-file-actions.tsx:181 and image-actions-menu.tsx:365, not a command to act on the name). 'Actions pour <name>' states exactly that 'for <asset>' relation. Verified independently that the same English string ships as 'Actions pour {name}' in ui.chat.canonical.link_toolkit.actions_for, ui.library.menu.asset_actions_label, ui.settings.appearance.editor.more and ui.shell.sidebar_navigation.row_actions — 5/5 renderings unanimous after this change, with the old 'sur' value the only outlier — and that 'sur' is used in this corpus only with a determiner-bearing generic noun ('Actions sur le fichier' x4, 'Actions sur l’image' x3, 'Actions sur l’élément', 'Actions sur le message'), with zero 'Actions sur <placeholder>' values in the entire fr catalogue. Grammar is stable for ANY inserted string: 'pour' needs no article, no gender agreement and no elision, so a name starting with a vowel ('Ébauche finale.png') or carrying quotes, punctuation, CJK or emoji slots in unchanged; no reordering of {name} is needed. Register: sentence case, capital 'Actions', no trailing punctuation, pure ASCII, no invisible or bidi characters, straight spaces; the fr guide's «…»-quoting rule is not triggered because neither the English nor any sibling {name} value quotes the inserted name. Fit: no maxCells hint in the sidecar (grep -c maxCells = 0 for the whole file), the string is an accessible name rather than a truncating container, and 19 characters is one more than the replaced value and shorter than the shipped generic neighbour 'Actions sur le fichier' (22). Note, not a finding: the same trigger's visible tooltip stays the generic 'Actions sur le fichier' / 'Actions sur l’image' in the other locale files of the pair, so users see 'sur' and screen readers hear 'pour'; that is the named/unnamed split the context sidecar prescribes and it is unchanged by this delta.
